text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging: KV cache blowup detected in cont-batching pool (us-west-2). High tail latency & CPU on batch-workers. Investigate.

jordan_oncall: seeing it. 90th/99th latencies spike, error rate up. attaching quick graph snapshots.

mira_eng_runtime: @jordan_oncall on it. Initial hypothesis: cache eviction storm causing repeated cache misses + long kv page fetch latencies -> batching queues balloon.

sam_sre: confirm infra metrics: node CPU across batch fleet at 85-95%, a few nodes >99%. Redis-like kvstore for page backend showing high read latencies (200-800ms).

jordan_oncall: does this correlate with recent config rollout? we pushed cont-batch config yesterday (max_batch_tokens increased from 2048->8192 on canary).

mira_eng_runtime: we did. Canary was limited to 5% but looks like traffic shard routing overlapped with certain tenant workloads -> bigger seq windows than expected.

nina_support: we have two customers reporting slow responses / timeouts. Raised severity with CS. Customer IDs: C-8812, C-9933.

jordan_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) rollback the batch_tokens change to previous value 2048; 2) reduce max_num_seqs from 128->32 as temporary; 3) enable conservative KV eviction throttle. Can someone apply hotfix to config service?

mira_eng_runtime: I'll prepare a quick hotfix. pushing patch to config-service: set cont_batch.max_batch_tokens=2048, cont_batch.max_num_seqs=32, kvcache.eviction_throttle=true. Will route to 10% then 100%.

devops-bot: deploy request queued: config-hotfix/412888-hf by mira_eng_runtime -> canary 10% -> runbook: rollback if 5xx > 1%. ETA ~2m.

jordan_oncall: good. Also temp scale up of pool by +20% to drain backlog. sam_sre can you handle autoscale?

sam_sre: scaling GPU batch-workers +20% now. watching queue depth.

mira_eng_runtime: applying hotfix now. diff:
```yaml
cont_batch:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_num_seqs: 32
kvcache:
  eviction_throttle: true
```

devops-bot: canary applied to 10% at 2026-03-15T09:42:15Z.

jordan_oncall: monitoring latency metrics and cache hit-rate. anyone see immediate improvement?

mira_eng_runtime: partial improvement: cache miss rate down ~30% on canary nodes, tail latency trending down. queue size on canary cut in half.

sam_sre: scaled workers are draining backlog. overall CPU dropping to ~70%.

nina_support: ping from C-8812: they're seeing response times improve, but intermittent failures persist. marking customer update sent.

allen_pm: flagging for priority comms. need to prep customer-facing summary once stabilized.

mira_eng_runtime: proceeding to roll hotfix to 100% in 3m if no regressions. watch for any 5xx spikes.

devops-bot: canary -> 100% rollout initiated.

jordan_oncall: post-rollout metrics look good so far. KV page fetch p95 down from 350ms -> 70ms.

sam_sre: no 5xx spike. continuing scaled-down nodes for 15m stabilization window.

mira_eng_runtime: follow-up: adding a short-term guard in runtime to reject requests that would create >8192 token batching windows (protective throttle) until we re-evaluate config defaults.

jordan_oncall: good. we should also add a circuit-breaker to avoid cascading cache evictions when miss rate exceeds threshold. Filed issue: ENG-RUNTIME-912.

nina_support: customer C-9933 confirms improved. sending closure note.

allen_pm: thanks team. Postmortem plan: capture timeline, config rollout path, routing overlap that caused canary to hit larger traffic shard, and action items: stricter canary routing checks, config gating on per-tenant seq histograms, add automatic rollback on miss-rate spikes. Owner: mira_eng_runtime + sam_sre.

mira_eng_runtime: will draft RCA. immediate action items: revert config default in repo, backfill canary tests, add metric alert for cont_batch.max_batch_tokens changes.

jordan_oncall: closing pager for now. leaving thread open for RCA drafts and customer comms drafts.

IncidentBot: Incident resolved (temporary mitigation applied). Tags: cont-batch, kvcache, rollout. Duration ~28m.

mira_eng_runtime: quick note for the RCA: logs show repeated `KVPageFetchTimeout` errors correlated with eviction waves. I'll attach sample logs to the doc.

sam_sre: adding system-level mitigations: ensure autoscaler cooldown higher for batch-workers to avoid oscillation during cache storms.

allen_pm: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and timeline. thanks everyone :v:
